name: HelloBench
ability_definition: The ability to communicate information and ideas in writing so others will understand.

task_realism.reasoning: Prompts come from real user requests across open-ended QA, summarization, chat, text completion and heuristic generation. That is a reasonable variety of explanatory and informational writing. However, the benchmark deliberately targets very long outputs, often thousands of words. Most workplace writing is shorter and audience-bound: emails, memos, reports, instructions. A sizable share of the tasks are creative or completion-style rather than communicating information to a specific reader.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Each response is a single shot at temperature 0.8 with no tools, retrieval, revision cycle, stakeholder context or defined recipient. Grading uses a GPT-4o judge applying checklists, with weights fitted to human ratings. No actual reader checks whether the intended information was understood. The emphasis on length can reward volume over concision. Workplace writing, by contrast, involves known audiences, source material, iteration and feedback.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The checklists capture some of the construct: content completeness, relevance, organization and instruction-following across several genres. Key parts of 'so others will understand' are missing or weak. There is no direct comprehension test, little audience adaptation, no testing of brevity or short-form clarity, and no persuasive or technical workplace documents with factual grounding. It measures sustained long-form generation quality more than communicative effectiveness.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are natural-language requests and outputs are free-form prose, which is structurally close to real writing artifacts. There is no multiple choice or toy format. The mismatch is the skew toward unusually long pieces and chat-style framing rather than typical document formats with conventions such as memos, briefs or emails.

transferability_reasoning: HelloBench asks for genuine open-ended prose from real user prompts and grades it with human-calibrated checklists, which gives it moderate relevance to Written Expression. Its transfer is limited by the focus on very long outputs, single-shot generation without audience or context, and an LLM judge rather than verified reader comprehension. It is best treated as a partial proxy for workplace writing ability.

2024.metric: HelloEval average score (checklist-weighted, roughly 0-100 points; higher is better)
2024.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: typical college-educated professionals who write explanations, summaries, reports and other extended texts as part of their jobs (not professional writers or editors)
